info.title: ManyPI API
info.description:
The REST API behind ManyPI — AI lead generation, email validation, cold-email outreach, agent runs and web scraping. Every endpoint is authenticated with a ManyPI API key (`mpi_...`) or an OAuth 2.1 access token, and honours the permissions granted to that credential.

API keys carry permissions per area of the API (Leads & companies, Campaigns, Inboxes & replies, Agents & skills, Scrapers & data, Account & usage), each set to Read or Read & write, plus separate permissions for actions that spend credits or reach the outside world: Run agents, Run scrapers, Verify email addresses, Send outreach and Invoke endpoints. Each operation below names what it needs. Keys with the older `read` and `write` permissions keep working everywhere.

tags.name: Leads
tags.description: Find, store, enrich and manage leads.

tags.name: Email validation
tags.description: Verify that lead addresses can receive mail.

tags.name: Outreach
tags.description: Inboxes, sequences, campaigns, sending and replies.

tags.name: Endpoints
tags.description: Publish scrapers as typed REST endpoints.

tags.name: Imports
tags.description: Bring campaigns, leads and the do-not-contact list over from another outreach tool.

get.description:
List and filter the workspace's leads, newest first. Also returns the declared custom columns, the lead searches that saved leads, the workspace total and the plan's lead limits, so a grid needs one call.

To get the leads one lead search found, pass its run id as `campaign`.

When the workspace is locked for billing, the response keeps the same shape but carries `billingLock`, and `leads` holds placeholder rows rather than real leads. Check for `billingLock` before you store or act on the rows.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read** (`leads:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text across company, full name, email and domain.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: A lifecycle status. `archived` and `unsubscribed` are still accepted as older spellings of `archived=only` and `subscribed=unsubscribed`.

parameters.name: campaign
parameters.description: The run id of a lead search: the `run_id` that `POST /api/leads/research` returns, or the id of any agent run that saved leads. Returns only the leads that search saved. `campaigns` in the `GET /api/leads` response lists the lead searches that have saved leads. A malformed id is ignored, so the request then returns every lead.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: Narrow to one brand by its id. Leave it out, or send `all`, for every brand you can reach. Leads with no brand are always included.

parameters.name: subscribed
parameters.description: Opt-out state, separate from `status`.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: `hide` leaves archived leads out, `show` includes them, `only` returns nothing else.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: `unassigned`, or a workspace member's user id.

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Only the leads in this lead list.

parameters.name: import
parameters.description: Only the leads one import created (`import_id` from `POST /api/leads/import`).

parameters.name: missing
parameters.description: Comma-separated keys, at most 20. Only leads where at least one of these core or custom fields is empty.

parameters.name: one_per_company
parameters.description: Keep only the best-ranked contact at each company. Leads with no company are always kept.

parameters.name: not_in_campaign
parameters.description: Leave out leads an outreach campaign holds or has mailed.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: A filter tree as JSON, the same one the leads grid builds.

parameters.name: tzo
parameters.description: Your timezone offset in minutes, for date filters in `filter`.

parameters.name: meta
parameters.description: Send `0` for rows only: `workspaceTotal` and `campaigns` are left out, which is faster when paging.

parameters.name: runs
parameters.description: Send `0` to leave out `campaigns` only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max 500.

workspaceTotal.description: Every lead the workspace stores, ignoring filters. Left out under `meta=0`.

campaigns.description: The lead searches that saved leads, newest first, with how many leads each saved. Pass an `id` as `campaign` to list its leads. Left out under `meta=0` or `runs=0`.

manualLeadLimit.description: How many leads a person may add by import or by hand. Higher than `leadLimit` on Free.

filterCapped.description: Present, and `true`, only when the filter was checked against the newest rows rather than all of them.

billingLock.description: Present only when the workspace is locked for billing. `leads` then holds placeholder rows and `total` is the number of real leads waiting behind the lock.

patch.description:
Change status and/or archive state for up to 500 leads at once.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

owner_id.description: Assign every lead to this workspace member. `null` unassigns.

category.description: A category key or name. `null` clears it.

schema.description: Send at least one of `status`, `archived`, `owner_id` or `category`.

400.description: Validation failed, or the category is unknown (`code: "unknown_category"`).

402.description: The workspace is locked for billing.

delete.description:
Permanently delete up to 500 leads. Consider archiving instead — archived leads stop appearing everywhere but stay recoverable.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

get.description:
Fetch one lead with its custom columns and email status.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read** (`leads:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

402.description: The workspace is locked for billing.

patch.description:
Update one field, the status, the score, or the archive flag on a single lead. Setting `field` to a name that is not a core field writes into the lead's custom columns.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

field.description: A core field (`company`, `full_name`, `title`, `email`, `phone`, `domain`, `linkedin_url`, `location`, `source_url`) or a custom column key. Also accepts `cc_emails` and `bcc_emails` (an array of addresses).

value.description: Empty string or null clears the field.

category.description: A category key or name. `null` clears it.

owner_id.description: Assign the lead to this workspace member. `null` unassigns.

brand_id.description: Move the lead to this brand.

400.description: Validation failed. `code` may be `invalid_recipient` (a bad cc or bcc address) or `unknown_category`.

402.description: The workspace is locked for billing.

403.description: The plan cannot create custom fields (`code: "lead_fields_locked"`), or you cannot reach that brand.

409.description: Another lead already has this email (`code: "duplicate_lead"`).

delete.description:
Permanently delete one lead.

The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not a lead with that id existed. To confirm the lead was there, fetch it first with `GET /api/leads/{id}`.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

post.description:
Launch the lead-generation agent against structured criteria, a saved search, or a set of seed leads ("find more like these").

The run is asynchronous: poll `GET /api/agents/runs/{id}` with the returned `run_id`. Once leads are saved, `GET /api/leads?campaign={run_id}` lists them. The run may pause with a clarifying question — answer it with `POST /api/agents/runs/{id}/reply` and the same run continues.

How many leads the run looks for comes from the description itself: "find 50 agencies" asks for 50. With no number it is 20, or 1 when the description names one company. One run finds at most 250, and never more than the workspace has room for. `criteria.count` is saved with a saved search and shown on it, but does not set the size of a run. When a number you stated was lowered, the response carries `clamped`. A full workspace returns `403` with `code: "lead_limit"`.

**With a saved search.** `criteria` sent alongside `profile_id` replaces the saved criteria as a whole — fields you leave out fall back to their defaults, not to the saved values. To change one field, read the saved search from `GET /api/leads/research-profiles`, merge your change, and send the full criteria. Because `save` defaults to `true`, the criteria you send are also written back to that saved search; send `save: false` to run without changing it.

**Two responses that start no lead search.** Both apply only to a typed request, with no `profile_id` and no `seed_lead_ids`:
- When `criteria` carries only a free-text `description` that does not read as a request for leads, ManyPI starts a plain agent run instead and the response includes `redirected: true`. Send `check_intent: false` to skip that check.
- When the description names leads the workspace already has, the response is `{ "known": {...}, "description": "..." }` with no `run_id`, and no run starts. Send `force_search: true` to search anyway.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

profile_id.description: Re-run a saved search. Its criteria are used when `criteria` is omitted; when `criteria` is sent, it replaces them entirely.

seed_lead_ids.description: Seed the search from existing leads ("find similar").

save.description: Persist the criteria as a reusable saved search. With `profile_id`, writes them back to that saved search.

check_intent.description: Check that a free-text-only request reads as a lead search, and start a plain agent run when it does not. Send `false` when your integration only ever sends lead searches.

force_search.description: Search even when the description names leads the workspace already has.

lead_list_id.description: File every lead this search saves into this lead list.

model.description: The model tier. `sol` needs a plan with the full models.

criteria.description: Find 25 e-commerce agencies building Shopify stores for DTC brands

200.description: A run was created — or, when `known` is present instead of `run_id`, the workspace already holds the leads the description names and no run was started.

count.description: How many leads this run looks for, after the limits above.

goal.description: The instruction the run was given.

context.description: The search criteria as data, as the app shows them.

clamped.description: Present only when the description stated a number and the run was held to fewer.

reason.description: `per_run` when one run's maximum was the limit, `plan` when the workspace's room was.

redirected.description: Present and `true` when the request did not read as a lead search and a plain agent run was started instead. See `check_intent`.

known.description: Present instead of `run_id` when the description names leads the workspace already has. Holds those leads; no run was started. See `force_search`.

description.description: The description that was matched, returned alongside `known`.

402.description: The workspace is locked for billing.

403.description: The workspace is storing all the leads the plan allows (`code: "lead_limit"`), or `extra_columns` names a column the plan cannot create (`code: "lead_fields_locked"`).

404.description: The saved search was not found.

get.description:
The workspace's saved lead searches, plus past lead-generation campaigns that were never saved as a profile.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read** (`leads:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

post.summary: Create or update a saved search
post.description:
Store a search without running it. Pass `id` to replace an existing profile in place: `criteria` replaces the stored criteria, and an omitted `name` is replaced by one generated from the criteria. To change only some fields — a rename, say — use `PATCH /api/leads/research-profiles/{id}`, which keeps whatever you leave out.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

patch.description:
Rename a saved search, change its kind, or replace its criteria. Anything you leave out keeps its stored value. `criteria`, when sent, replaces the stored criteria as a whole.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

delete.description:
Delete a saved search. Leads it already found are kept.

The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not a saved search with that id existed.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

post.description:
Company websites for a target such as "marketing agencies in Austin", found by ManyPI's own search. Directories, review sites, marketplaces, media and LinkedIn or Meta pages are left out, and each company appears once. Nothing is scanned: read the sites yourself, or with the ManyPI Chrome extension's Find companies.

Costs **1 crawl credit per results page**, whether or not the page held companies. Up to 5 pages per target.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

query.description: Who to find, in plain words.

country.description: Two-letter country code to search in, for example `de`.

skip.description: Domains you already have, left out of the answer.

200.description: Company sites on this results page.

next_page.description: The page to ask for next, or null after the last one.

sites.title: Northwind Studio | Brand agency in Austin
sites.snippet: Brand and web design for B2B companies.

400.description: The query is missing or too long, or there is no active workspace.

402.description: Out of crawl credits (`code: "crawl_credits_exhausted"`).

502.description: Search is unavailable right now (`code: "search_unavailable"`). Retry in a minute.

post.description:
Write a batch of leads. **Up to 100 rows per request** — chunk larger files client-side so a big import cannot outlive the request timeout and so progress is real.

`declare_fields` lets the same request that carries the first chunk also declare the custom columns those rows write into. It is idempotent, so resending the declarations with every chunk is harmless.

A full workspace still returns `200` — the rows that fitted were written — with `code: "lead_limit"` in the body.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

duplicates.description: `merge` fills blanks on the existing lead; `overwrite` lets incoming values win; `skip` leaves it untouched.

import_id.description: Omit on the first chunk; the response carries the id to send with every chunk after it, so all chunks land in one batch.

source.description: How the batch arrived, shown on it in the leads grid. First chunk only. `extension` is the ManyPI Chrome extension.

label.description: The batch name in the leads grid. First chunk only.

meta.description: Small facts about the batch only the sender knows, for example `{ "client": "chrome-extension", "version": "0.3.0", "scan": "site" }`. First chunk only, at most 4 KB.

skippedNoIdentity.description: No email and no domain-plus-name, so there is nothing to file the row under.

remaining.description: Lead slots left after this batch.

code.description: `lead_limit` when the workspace ran out of room, `import_limit` when the import passed 10,000 rows. The response is still `200`.

import_id.description: The import these rows were filed under. Use it as `import` on `GET /api/leads`, or send it back to add more rows to the same import.

leadIds.description: The leads created or updated. Not in input order.

rowLeadIds.description: One entry per input row, in input order: the lead it became, or `null` when it was skipped.

skippedOverImport.description: Rows past the 10,000-row limit for one import.

importLimit.description: Present when rows were skipped for the import limit.

402.description: The workspace is locked for billing.

403.description: `declare_fields` was sent on a plan without custom fields (`code: "lead_fields_locked"`).

Download the filtered leads as a file, up to 10,000 rows. Takes the same filters as `GET /api/leads`, so `campaign` exports the leads one lead search saved. Archived leads are left out unless you ask for them with `archived`.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read** (`leads:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

The same export as `GET /api/leads/export`, with the settings in a JSON body. Send `ids` to export exactly those leads (up to 10,000); otherwise the filters apply.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission. A read-only key cannot use this form; use the `GET` form instead.

get.description:
How many more leads the workspace can store. Read this before starting a large search or import — it changes every time a run saves a lead.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read** (`leads:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

remaining.description: `null` when the plan has no limit.

get.description:
The workspace's declared lead columns, in display order. These are column *definitions*; the values live on each lead's `custom` object.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read** (`leads:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

post.description:
Declare a column so leads can carry it. Set `auto_research` and the agent fills it in on future lead searches without you restating it each time.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

200.description: The column already existed and was returned unchanged.

403.description: The plan cannot create custom fields (`code: "lead_fields_locked"`).

post.description:
Queue an SMTP mailbox probe for lead addresses, raw addresses, or both. Results are written back onto the leads as `email_status`, `email_provider`, `email_is_role` and `email_validated_at`.

Pass `estimate_only` to price the run without queueing it. You are only charged for probes that actually run — cached results and addresses rejected by the cheap pre-check are free.

An API key needs the **Verify email addresses** permission (`leads:validate`). Write access to leads is not enough on purpose, so a general-purpose key cannot run up a validation bill.

lead_ids.description: Leads in this workspace whose addresses should be checked.

emails.description: Raw addresses, not tied to a lead.

campaign_id.description: Verify every lead actively enrolled in this campaign that has never been checked.

estimate_only.description: Price the run without queueing it.

schema.description: One job holds at most 5,000 distinct addresses across `lead_ids`, `emails` and `campaign_id` together. Addresses past that are dropped.

200.description: The job was queued, or (with `estimate_only`) priced.

schema.description: Two shapes. A normal call queues a job and returns `job_id`, `total` and `estimate`. An `estimate_only` call queues nothing and returns `estimate` alone — with no `job_id` and no `total` — so test for `job_id` before treating the response as a queued job.

freeUpFront.description: Addresses settled without a paid check, such as bad syntax.

alreadyCharged.description: Addresses checked recently enough that they are not charged again.

billable.description: Addresses that will use a validation credit.

402.description: Not enough validation credits, or the workspace is locked for billing.

get.description:
The workspace's recent validation jobs, newest first.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read** (`leads:read`), the **Verify email addresses** permission (`leads:validate`), or the legacy `read` permission.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Send `1` for queued and running jobs only.

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description: Send `1` for the jobs you started, rather than the whole workspace's.

get.description:
One validation job plus its per-address results. Poll this for progress and the final breakdown.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read** (`leads:read`), the **Verify email addresses** permission (`leads:validate`), or the legacy `read` permission.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: Set to `false` to omit the per-address results.

get.description:
Every connected sending identity with its health: today's sends versus the warmup-aware cap, 14-day delivered/failed/opened/bounced, a rolling 24-hour bounce rate, whether the bounce guard has paused it, and a 0–100 health score.

Use an inbox `id` as `smtp_config_id` when creating a campaign or sending.

An API key needs **Inboxes & replies: Read** (`inbox:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: Send `all` for every brand in the workspace. Any other value is ignored and your current brand is used.

get.description:
Saved email sequences with their inline steps. Brand-scoped; `?brand=all` widens to the whole workspace.

An API key needs **Campaigns: Read** (`outreach:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

post.description:
Create the email steps a campaign sends. Step 0 goes out on enrollment; each later step waits `wait_days` after the previous one and, with `thread_mode: "reply"`, threads under the first email. Merge variables: `{{first_name}}`, `{{company}}`, `{{title}}`, `{{domain}}`, `{{location}}`. Bodies are simple HTML — `

`, `
`, ``, ``. A/B variants inside a step require Pro or Business. An API key needs **Campaigns: Read & write** (`outreach:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

steps.description: Past 60 steps, or past the 10th email, steps are dropped without an error.

403.description: A/B variants require Pro or Business.

patch.description:
Rename a sequence or replace its steps. Send only what changes.

An API key needs **Campaigns: Read & write** (`outreach:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

403.description: A/B versions need the Pro or Business plan.

delete.description:
Delete a sequence. A sequence a campaign uses cannot be deleted: delete the campaign first.

An API key needs **Campaigns: Read & write** (`outreach:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

post.description:
AI-draft a cold email (`mode: "email"`) or a whole follow-up sequence (`mode: "sequence"`) from a plain-language brief, written against your brand context.

This only drafts: nothing is saved and nothing is sent. Feed the result into `POST /api/outreach/sequences` or `POST /api/outreach/send`.

An API key needs **Campaigns: Read & write** (`outreach:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

lead_id.description: An example lead to tailor the tone toward.

deal_id.description: With `mode: email`, write a follow-up for this CRM deal, with no merge variables.

example.instructions: We help e-commerce agencies find new client leads without cold-calling. Ask for a 15-minute call.

get.description:
Campaigns with per-campaign stats — enrolled, active, completed, sent, opened, replied — plus the sequence and inbox each is bound to.

An API key needs **Campaigns: Read** (`outreach:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: Send `all` for every brand in the workspace. Any other value is ignored and your current brand is used.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: `names` returns only `id`, `name`, `status` and `brand_id` per campaign, which is much faster. `content` returns each campaign's name and email steps.

campaigns.description: Each campaign also carries `replyStats`, `spark` (sends per day over 14 days), `inboxes`, `capacity` (its share of the inboxes it uses) and `work` (`remaining` emails, `tailDays` of waits still owed, `active` leads).

capacity.description: The workspace's sending headroom across its inboxes.

canSeeSentiment.description: Whether the plan includes reply sentiment.

post.description:
Create a campaign. Only `name` is required. With a sequence and at least one inbox it starts `active`; without either it is a `draft`, which goes live through `POST /api/outreach/campaigns/{id}/launch`. Then enroll leads with `POST /api/outreach/enroll`.

An API key needs **Campaigns: Read & write** (`outreach:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

smtp_config_id.description: An inbox id from `GET /api/outreach/inboxes`. Use `smtp_config_ids` for several.

smtp_config_ids.description: Send from several inboxes. The first is the primary.

brand_id.description: Create it in this brand rather than your current one.

status.description: Start paused or as a draft instead of active.

daily_limit.description: Never exceeds the inbox's own cap.

send_from.description: Local time, `HH:MM`. An invalid value is dropped without an error.

send_to.description: Local time, `HH:MM`. An invalid value is dropped without an error.

timezone.description: An IANA timezone such as `Europe/Berlin`. An unknown zone is dropped without an error.

priority.description: Higher wins the next paced slot when campaigns share an inbox. Values outside 1 to 10 are clamped, not rejected.

include_unsubscribe.description: Add an unsubscribe link to each email.

send_in_lead_timezone.description: Apply the send window on each lead's own clock.

404.description: The sequence, one of the inboxes, or the brand was not found.

patch.description:
Pause, resume or archive a campaign, or change its name, sequence, inboxes, reply-to, daily limit, schedule or priority. Send only what changes. Pausing stops further sends without losing progress.

Setting `status` to `active` resumes a paused campaign. It does not launch a draft: use `POST /api/outreach/campaigns/{id}/launch`.

An API key needs **Campaigns: Read & write** (`outreach:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

status.description: `active` resumes a paused campaign. A draft cannot be set active or archived here.

smtp_config_ids.description: Replace the inboxes it sends from. The first is the primary.

send_from.description: Local time, `HH:MM`. An invalid value is dropped.

send_to.description: Local time, `HH:MM`. An invalid value is dropped.

402.description: Resuming needs an active subscription. The workspace is locked for billing.

404.description: The campaign, sequence or inbox was not found.

409.description: `code` is `launch_required` (a draft cannot be set active here), `draft_not_archivable` (delete a draft instead), or `campaign_needs_inbox` (resuming needs a sending inbox).

delete.description:
Delete a campaign. Archiving (`PATCH` with `status: "archived"`) is usually the better choice — it keeps the history.

The campaign's sequence is deleted with it when no other campaign uses that sequence.

The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not a campaign with that id existed. To confirm it was there, fetch it first with `GET /api/outreach/campaigns/{id}`.

An API key needs **Campaigns: Read & write** (`outreach:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

200.description: Deleted, or there was nothing to delete.

get.description:
One campaign's full analytics: headline stats, a per-step breakdown, the newest 500 enrollments with their progress, a daily timeline, A/B results, the funnel and the reply mix.

The per-step breakdown is where you see whether the follow-ups are doing the work.

An API key needs **Campaigns: Read** (`outreach:read`), or the legacy `read` permission.

post.description:
Queue the campaign's sequence for real sending, respecting the inbox's warmup and daily caps. Up to 1,000 leads per call; ids past the first 1,000 are counted in `skipped_over_limit`.

Skipped rather than failed: leads with no email, leads already enrolled, unsubscribed or suppressed addresses, addresses that bounced, addresses known to be undeliverable, and — when the brand only writes to confirmed addresses — addresses that could not be confirmed. Each cause has its own counter; `summary` explains them in plain language.

When the brand has *validate on enroll* turned on (the default), unchecked addresses are enrolled and checked in the background (`queued_for_validation`). The result is applied at send time, so an address that turns out undeliverable is never sent to.

**Sending cannot be undone.** Requires a paid plan. An API key needs the **Send outreach** permission (`outreach:send`).

schema.description: Skips are reported as one counter per cause rather than a single total. Counters for causes that did not occur may be omitted. For the number of leads that were not enrolled, add up every `skipped_*` counter and `already_enrolled` — or compute `requested - enrolled`.

Find their address first, then add them again. 3 leads unsubscribed, so they stay on your do-not-contact list. Remove them from Suppressions if that was a mistake. 2 leads bounced the last time you wrote. Sending again would only damage the reputation of the inbox you send from.

On those other plans the `sentiment` filter is **ignored, not rejected**: every reply comes back, and the response says `canSeeSentiment: false`. Check that flag before treating the results as filtered — otherwise, say, every reply gets routed as positive.

post.description:
Deliver a message into a run.

- **Paused run** — the reply is submitted as the answer to the agent's pending question and the *same* run continues mid-thought.
- **Finished run** (`completed` / `failed` / `cancelled`) — a follow-up run starts in the same conversation, inheriting its context and playbook, so "find 25 more like those" keeps saving leads.
- **Still working**: the message is queued and the run keeps its progress. With `mode: queued` (the default) the agent reads it when it next comes up for air; with `mode: now` it arrives at the next step. The response has `status: "interjected"`. Pass `interrupt: true` instead to cancel the run and start a new one with your message.

An API key needs the **Run agents** permission (`agents`).

post.description:

Runs that already finished (`completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`) are left as they are. The response is `{ "ok": true }` in every case, including for an id that matches no run — read the run with `GET /api/agents/runs/{id}` to see its status.

An API key needs the **Run agents** permission (`agents`).

Check a key for another outreach tool and scan that account, before anything is imported. Opens an import in status `scanned` that holds the scan; `POST /api/integrations/migrations/{id}` starts it.

Supported tools and the credentials each takes:

| `provider` | `credentials` |
| --- | --- |
| `instantly` | `api_key` (an API V2 key) |
| `smartlead` | `api_key` |
| `lemlist` | `api_key` |
| `apollo` | `api_key` (a master key, for sequences to come over) |
| `snovio` | `client_id`, `client_secret` |
| `saleshandy` | `api_key` |

Only the fields a tool takes are kept. The key is stored encrypted on the import and erased when the import finishes or is cancelled. It is never returned.

To import contacts from a CRM or support tool already connected under **Integrations** (HubSpot, Pipedrive, Attio, Close, Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk), send `connection_id` instead. The connection's stored credentials are used and nothing is pasted.

An API key needs the legacy `write` permission. Keys made with per-area permissions cannot call this route yet.

post.description:
Say what to bring and start. The order is fixed: the do-not-contact list first, so nothing that arrives later is queued before its opt-out is known; then the chosen campaigns, recreated as **draft** campaigns with their email steps; then their leads, with custom variables as lead fields.

Nothing is sent. The campaigns stay drafts with no inbox until you launch them in ManyPI. With `enrollNotContacted`, leads the old tool never emailed are queued in their new campaign, so the sequence carries on once it is launched. Leads that replied, bounced or unsubscribed are never queued.

The first slice runs inside this request, so the response already shows progress. After that the import runs in slices: call `POST /api/integrations/migrations/{id}/advance` until `status` is `done`. An import nobody advances is picked up by ManyPI's scheduler, a few seconds every five minutes, so it finishes either way.

Only campaign ids the scan found are used; others are dropped. Calling this on an import that is not `scanned` returns it unchanged.

At most 100,000 leads per import, and the plan's lead allowance applies (leads over it are counted in `overLimit`). Custom fields need the Starter plan and queuing leads needs a paid plan; without them the import still runs and says what stayed behind in `warnings`.

An API key needs the legacy `write` permission. Keys made with per-area permissions cannot call this route yet.

Stop an import that has not finished and erase its stored key. What already came over stays: leads, draft campaigns and do-not-contact entries are not removed. A cancelled import cannot be resumed; scan again to start a new one. An import that already finished is returned unchanged.

An API key needs the legacy `write` permission. Keys made with per-area permissions cannot call this route yet.

post.description:
Run the next slice of a running import, about 15 seconds of work, and return where it stands. Call it in a loop until `job.status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

`worked: false` means another slice held the import at that moment (the scheduler, or a second caller), the other tool asked for a pause, or the import has finished. Nothing is lost; ask again a few seconds later.

Every slice is safe to repeat. Leads dedupe on the same identity the CSV import uses, do-not-contact entries skip what is already listed, and queued leads and campaigns are never created twice.

An API key needs the legacy `write` permission. Keys made with per-area permissions cannot call this route yet.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The import id, from `POST /api/integrations/migrations`.

worked.description: False when nothing ran in this call.

402.description: The workspace is locked for billing (past due or ended plan).

get.summary: Validate a key / get account info
get.description:
The quickest way to confirm a key works. Returns the owning user, the workspace and brand these credentials act in (where imported leads land) and, for an API key, its permissions and rate limit. Accepts an API key or an OAuth access token.

An API key needs **Account & usage: Read** (`account:read`), or the legacy `read` permission. A key without it gets `403`, so a key made only for scrapers or outreach fails this check even though it works on its own routes.

brand.description: The brand inside the workspace. Imported leads land here.

apiKey.description: Present when an API key was used, null for an OAuth token.

403.description: This API key does not have the permission this route needs.

404.description: No profile exists for this account.

patch.description:
Change a column's label, type, choices, colours, description, research setting or position. Send only what changes. The `key` never changes, so stored values stay attached.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

type.description: Switching away from `select` or `multi_select` clears the choices.

delete.description:
Remove a custom column. Its values are cleared from every lead unless you send `keep_values=1`, which keeps them in the lead data without a column.

An API key needs **Leads & companies: Read & write** (`leads:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

post.description:
Make a draft campaign live. This is the only way a draft starts sending. It checks everything at once: a sequence with written emails, a sending inbox, at least one lead, and a plan that can send. When something is missing the response is `409` with every issue listed.

**Sending starts right away for leads already enrolled.** An API key needs the **Send outreach** permission (`outreach:send`).

402.description: The workspace is locked for billing.

403.description: Sending needs the Starter plan or above (`code: "outreach_locked"`).

example.error: This campaign is not ready to launch yet.

get.description:
What a run did, step by step: each tool call, result and message, in order. Pass the `seq` of the last event you have as `after` to get only newer ones.

An API key needs **Agents & skills: Read** (`agents:read`), the **Run agents** permission (`agents`), or the legacy `read` permission.

402.description: The workspace is locked for billing.

patch.description:
Change one of your own skills. ManyPI's premade skills cannot be changed.

An API key needs **Agents & skills: Read & write** (`agents:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

delete.description:
Delete one of your own skills. The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not anything was deleted.

An API key needs **Agents & skills: Read & write** (`agents:write`), or the legacy `write` permission.

200.description: Deleted, or there was nothing to delete.

bearerAuth.description: A ManyPI API key (`mpi_...`) from the profile menu → API Access in the dashboard, or an OAuth 2.1 access token obtained through the MCP consent flow.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired credential, or an API key without the permission this route needs. Both look the same, so check the key's permissions under API Access when a key that worked elsewhere is refused. A few routes check the key themselves and answer `403` instead.

BadRequest.description: The request body or parameters failed validation.

NotFound.description: No such resource in this workspace.

EndpointResult.description: The extracted data, matching the endpoint's output schema. `X-ManyPI-Cache` says whether it came from the cache (`hit`) or a fresh scrape (`miss`); `X-ManyPI-Run-Id` names the run behind it.

X-ManyPI-Cached-At.description: When the cached result was produced. Sent on cache hits only.

EndpointAccepted.description: Still running — the endpoint is `async`, or the scrape ran past the ~110 second inline budget. Poll the URL in `poll` (also sent as `Location`) with `GET /v1/e/{slug}/results/{runId}`.

poll.description: Path of the result to poll, e.g. `/v1/e/{slug}/results/{runId}`.

EndpointFailed.description: The scrape failed (`error: "Scrape failed"`), or it finished but the result did not match the endpoint's output schema. In the second case `details` lists the mismatches and `raw` carries the result that was produced — the credits for it are already spent.

campaigns.description: Campaign ids from `scan.campaigns`. Leads are read through these campaigns, so for lemlist and Smartlead a lead in no chosen campaign stays behind; Instantly also brings leads that sit in lists, and Apollo, Snov.io and Saleshandy bring every contact.

recreateCampaigns.description: Recreate the chosen campaigns as drafts with their email steps.

doNotContact.description: Bring the block list, plus leads that bounced or unsubscribed there.

enrollNotContacted.description: Queue leads the old tool never emailed into their new draft campaign. Needs `recreateCampaigns` and a paid plan.

duplicates.description: A lead that already exists: `merge` fills in only its empty fields, `overwrite` replaces its fields, `skip` leaves it alone.

asCustomers.description: Contact imports: also put every imported address on do-not-contact (existing customers).

provider.description: The tool imported from, e.g. `instantly` or `hubspot`.

account_label.description: The account as the other tool names it.

status.description: The other tool's own word for it.

leadsTotal.description: Null when the tool cannot count cheaply.

listLeads.description: Leads that sit in lists rather than campaigns (Instantly only).

accounts.description: Sending mailboxes in the other tool. They are listed, not moved.

notes.description: Worth knowing before starting, e.g. a key that cannot read sequences.

campaignMap.description: Other tool's campaign id to ManyPI campaign id.

suppressed.description: Addresses and domains added to do-not-contact.

skipped.description: Rows not written: duplicates, rows with no email or other identity, and conflicts.

overLimit.description: Leads left out because the plan's lead allowance was full.

enrolled.description: Leads queued in their new draft campaign.

customFields.description: Custom variables created as lead fields.

skippedSteps.description: Per ManyPI campaign, steps that could not come over, e.g. `2 LinkedIn steps`.

importIds.description: Other tool's campaign id (`_` for leads in no campaign) to the ManyPI import id. Use one as `import` on `GET /api/leads`.

strikes.description: Failures in a row on the current step.

result.description: Set when the import ends: `counts`, `campaignMap`, `warnings` and `skippedSteps`, as in `progress`.

error.description: Why a `failed` import stopped. What came over before it is kept.
Human-readable message. A few validation failures (creating or updating an endpoint, bulk lead updates and deletes) send a list of the individual problems here instead of one string.

code.description: A machine-readable code on gated failures: `lead_limit`, `outreach_locked`, `validation_credits_exhausted`.

details.description: Extra detail on some failures, such as the list of parameters that failed an endpoint's `param_schema`.

custom.description: Values for the workspace's declared custom columns.

agent_run_id.description: The lead search that produced this lead.

list_ids.description: The lead lists this lead is in.

reply_summary.description: List responses only. What this lead has replied, if anything.

email_guess.description: List responses only. The checked guesses for a lead with no confirmed email.

options.description: The choices of a `select` or `multi_select` column.

auto_research.description: The agent fills this in on future lead searches.

key.description: Derived from the label when absent.

option_colors.description: A colour per choice. Unknown colour names are dropped.

ImportRow.description: A row is skipped only when email, domain, full_name and company are all empty.

custom.description: Keys (at most 40 characters) must match declared columns, or the values are dropped.

LeadResearchCriteria.description: The structured search. The description does most of the work; the rest is what the agent enforces.

count.description: Saved with a saved search and shown on it. It does not set the size of a run: state the number in `description` instead, e.g. "Find 50 ...".

company_size.description: Free text on purpose: "5-50 employees", "Series A", "under $5M ARR".

titles.description: Roles to reach inside each company.

exclusions.description: Hard excludes — matches are dropped, not saved.

required_fields.description: A lead missing one of these is not saved.

extra_columns.description: Extra researched columns, written to the lead's custom fields.

sources.description: Where to look: directories, marketplaces, maps, specific sites.

construct_emails.description: Work out missing addresses from the company's pattern. `null` uses the brand setting.

contact_preference.description: `personal` skips shared inboxes like info@. `null` uses the brand setting.

use_brand_icp.description: Also judge fit against the brand's own customer profile.

similar_to.description: Seed leads for a "find similar" search. Filled in from `seed_lead_ids`.

counts.description: How many addresses landed in each status.

name.description: The inbox label, which is often the address itself.

from.description: The sending address. Falls back to the SMTP username when no from-address is set.

sent24h.description: Sends in the last rolling 24 hours — the window `cap` applies to.

cap.description: Warmup-aware cap for the current window, not the raw daily limit.

dailyLimit.description: The inbox's configured daily limit, before warmup is applied.

bounceRate14d.description: Percentage to one decimal place: `9.2` means 9.2%.

warmingUp.description: True while the inbox is still ramping and `cap` is below `dailyLimit`.

sendingPausedAt.description: Set when the bounce guard paused the inbox.

health.description: Delivery success rate, capped at 94 while warming up and reduced four points per percent of 14-day bounce rate.

free.description: Sends still free today after its campaigns' share.

warmupDays.description: Days to full volume, when warming up.

warmupDay.description: Which warmup day it is on.

subject.description: Merge variables allowed. Empty on a `reply` step, which sends as "Re:" the first email's subject.

wait_days.description: Days after the previous step, up to 90. Fractions work: `0.5` is 12 hours. Step 0 is 0.

variants.description: Up to 4 extra A/B versions of this step. Pro and Business only.

paused_variants.description: Indexes of versions that stop sending. `0` is the step's own text.

tailor_body.description: How much of the body is personalized per lead.

smtp_config_id.description: Send this step from a specific inbox.

status.description: A campaign without a sequence or an inbox starts as `draft`. A draft goes live only through `POST /api/outreach/campaigns/{id}/launch`.

send_days.description: Weekdays to send on, as `Date.getDay()` numbers: 0 is Sunday, 1 is Monday, 6 is Saturday. Values outside 0-6 are discarded, so an ISO-style Sunday of 7 is dropped rather than honoured. Defaults to `[1,2,3,4,5]` when omitted, or when every supplied value is discarded.

inbox_strategy.description: How sends are spread when several inboxes are available.

include_unsubscribe.description: Whether an unsubscribe link is appended to each email.

require_verified.description: Whether unverified addresses are validated before enrollment.

unsubscribed_sends.description: Sends that went to an address which later opted out.

sentiment.description: Pro and Business only; stripped from the response on other plans.

result_summary.description: The result — or, while `paused`, the agent's question to you.

download_url.description: Signed URL, valid for one hour.

added.description: Whether it shows in your skill picker. Your own skills always do.

scraper_schema.description: The JSON Schema the extracted data conforms to.

ScraperRun.description: A scraper run as returned by `GET /api/runs`. The extracted data is also spread onto the root of each run, so a completed run carries that scraper's own fields alongside the ones below; the fields here win on a name collision.

result.description: The extracted data. Null until the run completes.

downloadUrl.description: Storage path for the full JSON result.
